data.name: Advait
data.gender_notes: Advait is used as a male name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit a, 'not', + dvaita, 'duality' — 'non-dual'. Its root is Sanskrit a + dvaita. The Vedantic doctrine of non-dualism. Advait is a Sanskrit name meaning “Non-dual; unique; without a second”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Advait expresses “Non-dual; unique; without a second”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Advait total 21, reducing to 3. Number 3 is associated with expression, creativity and optimism.

vedic_reference.note: Advaita is a philosophical concept in Hinduism, Jainism, and Buddhism, which asserts the ultimate reality is non-dual or non-plural. In Hinduism, it is associated with the Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, and the works of Shankara and Ramanuja.
